captions: You're in the middle of something important.
Then *NEPA* takes the light.
You check the meter.
They didn't take it o — it was *your units* that finished.
And just when you think you're done,
MTN sends you a message: your data is down to *50MB* too.
So now you're deciding what to pay for *between the two*.
These are *competing household needs*.
Automatic payments can follow instructions,
but they don't know which need *matters more right now*.
So we built *Borderless*.
An autonomous household utilities agent.
You set your household *budget*, *priorities* and spending permissions.
You set the rules. *Borderless does the work.*
But here's where Borderless differs from *ordinary auto-pay*.
Imagine you have just *2 USDC* of spending authority left.
Your electricity is running low.
Your mobile data is running low too.
Both matter. But you can't afford both right now.
Borderless weighs the household's *priorities*, urgency and eligible options.
It prioritises *electricity* and defers the data purchase.
And it explains why.
One decision matters most: the agent does not control *financial authority*.
Every intended purchase passes through an *independent policy engine*.
Only then can the purchase reach the *x402* payment layer.
The provider protects the resource behind *HTTP 402*.
Borderless validates the terms; the facilitator verifies and *settles on Stellar*.
Only after settlement does the provider *release* the resource.
We simulate a low electricity balance.
Borderless detects the shortage, checks its spending authority
and discovers an eligible electricity provider.
It requests the purchase.
The provider responds: *HTTP 402, Payment Required*.
It won't release the protected resource until payment is *verified*.
Borderless validates the terms against the household's permissions.
It's within the authorised limit, so it proceeds.
Using *x402 on Stellar*, it makes a real USDC payment on testnet.
The provider verifies the settlement and *releases* the purchase.
The simulated meter is credited. Borderless verifies fulfilment
and generates a *receipt*.
Here, it attempts a purchase above the authorised limit.
The system rejects it *before payment is signed*.
Because autonomy should never mean *losing control*.
We started with *electricity*. The same system extends to airtime, data and more.
This is Borderless.
Your household stays powered and connected. *Borderless handles the rest.*
Made by Gloria and Hannah.
